Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sent him to hire a guide (to take them to Madinah) and Hadhrat Aaamir (RA) hired a man called Ibnul Ayqadh. He belonged to the Banu Abd bin Adi tribe who were allies of the Banu Sahm branch of the Banu Aas bin Waa'il tribe that belonged to the Quraysh. This guide from the Banu Adi tribe was a Mushrik then and it was his occupation to guide people on the journeys. During those nights (that they hid the cave), the two of them (Hadhrat Aamir (RA) and the guide) hid in the camels of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) while Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) would come to them every evening and relate to them the events taking place in Makkah. Every night, Hadhrat Aamir (RA) would bring them some goats, which they would milk and then slaughter one to eat. Early in the mornings, he would take the goats away to the grazing fields that the people used for their goats and no one realised what was happening.
This continued until talk of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) died down and they learnt that things were quiet. Their two companions then arrived with the camels and they left. They had already been in the cave for two days and two nights. They took Hadhrat Aamir bin Fuhayra (RA) along with them, who drove the camels, served them and assisted them. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) would let him ride the camel behind him in turns. Besides Hadhrat Aamir (RA) and the guide from the Banu Adi, no one else accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). [^1]
The preparations that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) made for the Hijrah

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never failed to visit Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) during one of the ends of the day. He either visited during the mornings or during the evenings. This was his practice until the day arrived when Allaah permitted him to migrate and to leave Makkah in the midst of all the people. That day, Rasulullaah ﷺ came to our house at midday which was a time that he usually never visited. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) saw him come, he said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ will come during this hour only if something important has cropped up.' When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) moved back on his bed (to make way for him) and Rasulullaah ﷺ sat down. There was nobody with Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) besides myself and my sister Asmaa bint Abi Bakr. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Send everyone else away from you.' Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, 'It is only my two daughters. May my parents be sacrificed for you, there is no harm in them being here.'"
Narrating further, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'Allaah has permitted me to migrate and to leave Makkah.' Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked, 'May I accompany you?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'You may
